translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year he concurrently served as Prefect of Jingzhao; his commissioner posts all as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year he concurrently served as prefect of Jingzhao while retaining his commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 鉷威權轉盛，兼二十餘使，近宅為使院，文案堆積，胥吏求押一字，即累日不遂。

translations.literal: Hong's authority and power grew ever greater; he concurrently held more than twenty commissioner posts. Near his residence he made a commissioner office; documents piled up, and clerks seeking one character of seal might wait many days without success.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's power grew ever greater. He held more than twenty commissioner posts at once. He set up a commissioner office near his residence; documents piled up, and clerks seeking a single seal might wait days without success.

sentences.zh: 中使賜遺，不絕於門，雖晉公林甫亦畏避之。

translations.literal: Palace envoys' gifts and presents did not cease at his gate; even Duke of Jin Linfu also feared and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys bearing gifts never ceased at his gate. Even Li Linfu, Duke of Jin, feared and avoided him.

sentences.zh: 林甫子岫為將作監，供奉禁中；

translations.literal: Linfu's son Xiu was Director of Palace Construction, attending within the forbidden precinct;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu's son Xiu was director of palace construction and attended within the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 鉷子準衛尉少卿，亦鬥雞供奉，每謔岫，岫常下之。

translations.literal: Hong's son Zhun was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud, also attending with cockfighting; he always mocked Xiu, and Xiu usually came off worse.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Zhun was vice director of the Court of Imperial Stud and also attended with cockfighting. He always mocked Xiu, who usually came off worse.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉韋黃裳、長安尉賈季鄰常於廳事貯錢數百繩，名倡珍饌，常有備擬，以候準所適。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wannian Wei Huangshang and Magistrate of Chang'an Jia Jilin often stored several hundred strings of cash in the hall office, famous singers and rare delicacies always kept in readiness, to await wherever Zhun might go.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Huangshang, magistrate of Wannian, and Jia Jilin, magistrate of Chang'an, often kept hundreds of strings of cash in their offices along with famous singers and fine food, always ready wherever Zhun might go.

sentences.zh: 又於宅側自有追歡之所。

translations.literal: Again beside the residence he had his own place for pursuing pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Beside his residence he also kept his own house of pleasure.

sentences.zh: 鉷與弟戶部郎中銲，召術士任海川遊其門，問其相命，言有王否。

translations.literal: Hong and his younger brother Director of the Ministry of Revenue Han summoned the adept Ren Haichuan to visit his gate and asked about his physiognomy and fate, speaking of whether there was kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and his younger brother Han, director of the Ministry of Revenue, summoned the adept Ren Haichuan and asked about his physiognomy and fate, inquiring whether kingship was indicated.

sentences.zh: 海川震懼，潛匿不出。

translations.literal: Haichuan was shaken with fear and secretly hid without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Haichuan was terrified and hid himself, refusing to come out.

sentences.zh: 鉷懼泄其事，令逐之，至馮翊郡，得，誣以他事杖殺之。

translations.literal: Hong feared the matter would leak; he ordered pursuit, and at Fupi Commandery he was captured, falsely charged with another matter, and beaten to death with the stick.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the matter would leak, Hong ordered him pursued. He was captured in Fupi Commandery, falsely charged with another offense, and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 定安公主男韋會任王府司馬，聞之，話於私庭，乃被侍兒說於傭保者。

translations.literal: Princess of Ding'an's son Wei Hui served as Military Affairs Official of the Prince's Establishment; hearing of it, he spoke of it in a private courtyard, and a maid told the hired guards.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hui, son of Princess of Ding'an and military affairs official of a princely establishment, heard of it and spoke of it privately. A maid told the hired guards.

sentences.zh: 或有憾於會，告於鉷，鉷遣賈季鄰收於長安獄，入夜縊之，明辰載屍還其家。

translations.literal: Someone who bore a grudge against Hui reported to Hong; Hong sent Jia Jilin to seize him in Chang'an prison, strangled him at night, and the next morning carried the corpse back to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who bore a grudge against Hui reported to Hong. Hong sent Jia Jilin to seize him in Chang'an prison, strangled him at night, and the next morning returned his corpse to his home.

sentences.zh: 會皇堂外甥，同產兄王繇尚永穆公主，而惕息不敢言。

translations.literal: Hui was maternal nephew of the imperial clan; his full brother Wang Yao married Princess of Yongmu, yet he trembled and did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a maternal nephew of the imperial clan; his full brother Wang Yao had married Princess of Yongmu. Yet he trembled and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 十載，封太原縣公，又兼殿中監。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan County and again concurrently served as Director of the Palace Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan County and again concurrently served as director of the palace department.

sentences.zh: 十一載四月，銲與故鴻臚少卿邢璹子縡情密累年，縡潛構逆謀，引右龍武軍萬騎刻取十一月殺龍武將軍，因燒諸城門及市，分數百人殺楊國忠及右相李林甫、左相陳希烈等。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Han and the son of former Vice Minister of Ceremonial Xing Suo, Zao, had been intimate for many years; Zao secretly formed a treasonous plot, drawing the Ten Thousand Riders of the Right Dragon Martial Guard to set a date in the eleventh month to kill the Dragon Martial general, then burn the various city gates and markets, and divide several hundred men to kill Yang Guozhong and Right Chief Minister Li Linfu, Left Chief Minister Chen Xilie, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year Han and Zao, son of former vice minister of ceremonial Xing Suo, had been intimate for years. Zao secretly formed a treasonous plot, drawing the Ten Thousand Riders of the Right Dragon Martial Guard to set a date in the eleventh month to kill the Dragon Martial general, burn the city gates and markets, and send several hundred men to kill Yang Guozhong, Right Chief Minister Li Linfu, Left Chief Minister Chen Xilie, and others.

sentences.zh: 先期二日事發，玄宗臨朝，召鉷，上於玉案前過狀與鉷。

translations.literal: Two days before the appointed time the affair was exposed; Xuanzong held court, summoned Hong, and passed the report before the jade desk to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before the appointed time the plot was exposed. Xuanzong held court, summoned Hong, and passed the report across the jade desk to him.

sentences.zh: 鉷好弈棋，縡善棋，鉷因銲與之交故，至是意銲在縡處金城坊，密召之，日晏，始令捕賊官捕之。

translations.literal: Hong loved chess; Zao was skilled at chess. Hong, because of Han's friendship with Zao, at this point thought Han was at Zao's place in Jincheng Ward; he secretly summoned him, and when the day was late he only then ordered the arresting officials to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong loved chess; Zao was skilled at it. Because of Han's friendship with Zao, Hong thought Han was at Zao's place in Jincheng Ward and secretly summoned him. Not until late in the day did he order officials to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉薛榮光、長安尉賈季鄰等捕之，逢銲於化度寺門。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wannian Xue Rongguang, Magistrate of Chang'an Jia Jilin, and others pursued and seized him, meeting Han at the gate of Huadu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rongguang, magistrate of Wannian, Jia Jilin, magistrate of Chang'an, and others pursued him and met Han at the gate of Huadu Temple.

sentences.zh: 季鄰為鉷所引用，為赤尉，銲謂之曰：「我與邢縡故舊，縡今反，恐事急妄相引，請足下勿受其言。」

translations.literal: Jilin, whom Hong had promoted and employed, was a red-uniformed magistrate; Han said to him: 'Zao and I are old friends; Zao is now in rebellion—I fear that in urgency he may falsely implicate me. I ask you, sir, not to accept his words.'"
translations.idiomatic: Jilin, whom Hong had promoted, was a red-uniformed magistrate. Han told him, 'Zao and I are old friends. He is now in rebellion, and I fear that in urgency he may falsely implicate me. Please do not accept his words.'"

sentences.zh: 榮先等至縡門，縡等十餘人持弓刃突出，榮先等遂與格戰。

translations.literal: Rongguang and the others reached Zao's gate; Zao and more than ten men holding bows and blades burst out, and Rongguang and the others thereupon fought with them.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang and the others reached Zao's gate. Zao and more than ten men with bows and blades burst out, and they fought.

sentences.zh: 季鄰以銲語白鉷，鉷肐謂之曰：「我弟何得與之有謀乎！」

translations.literal: Jilin reported Han's words to Hong; Hong glared and said to him: 'How could my younger brother have plotted with them!'"
translations.idiomatic: Jilin reported Han's words to Hong. Hong glared and said, 'How could my younger brother have plotted with them!'"

sentences.zh: 鉷與國忠共討逐縡，縡下人曰：「勿損太夫人。」

translations.literal: Hong and Guozhong jointly pursued and drove out Zao; Zao's subordinates said: 'Do not harm the Grand Lady.'
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Guozhong jointly pursued Zao. Zao's followers cried, 'Do not harm the Grand Lady.'

sentences.zh: 國忠為劍南節度使，有隨身官以白國忠曰：「賊有號，不可戰。」

translations.literal: Guozhong was Military Governor of Jiannan; an attendant official accompanying him reported to Guozhong, saying: 'The rebels have a battle cry—do not fight.'"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was military governor of Jiannan. An attendant reported to him, 'The rebels have a battle cry—do not fight.'"

sentences.zh: 須臾，驃騎大將軍、內侍高力士領飛龍小兒甲騎四百人討之，縡為亂兵所斬，擒其黨善射人韋瑤等以獻。

translations.literal: Before long, Flying Dragon General of the Inner Palace Attendant Gao Lishi led four hundred armored horsemen of the Flying Dragon youths to suppress them; Zao was cut down by the disorderly soldiers, and his party the skilled archer Wei Yao and others were captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Flying Dragon General and palace attendant Gao Lishi led four hundred armored Flying Dragon youths against them. Zao was cut down by the disorderly soldiers, and his follower the skilled archer Wei Yao and others were captured and presented.

sentences.zh: 國忠以白玄宗，玄宗以鉷委任深，必不與之知情，鉷與銲別生，嫉其富貴，故欲陷鉷耳，遂特原銲不問，然意欲鉷請罪之。

translations.literal: Guozhong reported this to Xuanzong; Xuanzong thought Hong was deeply entrusted and certainly could not have known of it with him—Hong and Han were born of different mothers, and Han envied his wealth and honor, therefore wishing to trap Hong—thereupon he specially pardoned Han without inquiry, yet his intent was that Hong should plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong reported to Xuanzong. Xuanzong thought Hong was too deeply trusted to have known of the plot—Hong and Han were half-brothers, and Han envied his wealth and wished to trap him—so he specially pardoned Han without inquiry, yet expected Hong to plead guilty.

sentences.zh: 上密令國忠諷之，國忠不敢泄上意，諷鉷曰：「且主上眷大夫深，今日大夫須割慈存門戶，但抗疏請罪郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly ordered Guozhong to hint to him; Guozhong did not dare reveal the emperor's intent and hinted to Hong, saying: 'Moreover the ruler favors the Grandee deeply; today the Grandee must sever affection to preserve the household gate—only submit a memorial pleading guilty for the Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered Guozhong to hint to Hong. Guozhong dared not reveal the emperor's intent and told Hong, 'The ruler favors you deeply. Today you must sever affection to preserve your house—submit a memorial pleading guilty for the director.

sentences.zh: 郎中亦未必至極刑，大夫必存，何如並命！」

translations.literal: The Director also may not necessarily reach extreme punishment; the Grandee will certainly be preserved—how is that compared with dying together!"
translations.idiomatic: The director may not necessarily face the extreme penalty; you will certainly be preserved—how is that compared with dying together!"

sentences.zh: 鉷俯首久曰：「小弟先人餘愛，平昔頻有處分，義不欲捨之而謀存。」

translations.literal: Hong bowed his head for a long time and said: "My younger brother is my late father's remaining affection; in ordinary times I have often made allowances for him—in duty I cannot abandon him to plot preservation."
translations.idiomatic: Hong bowed his head a long time and said, "My younger brother is my late father's remaining affection. I have often indulged him—I cannot abandon him to save myself."

sentences.zh: 乃進狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 十二日，鉷入朝，左相陳希烈言語侵之，鉷恨之，憤訴言氣頗高。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day Hong entered court; Left Chief Minister Chen Xilie's words insulted him; Hong resented it and complained in anger, his tone rather high.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day Hong entered court. Left Chief Minister Chen Xilie insulted him; Hong resentfully complained in an angry, high tone.

sentences.zh: 鉷朝回，於中書侍郎廳修表，令人進狀，門司已不納矣。

translations.literal: Hong returned from court and at the Vice Director of the Secretariat's hall revised his memorial; he had someone submit the memorial—the gate office would no longer accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from court, Hong revised his memorial in the vice director of the Secretariat's hall and had someone submit it, but the gate office would no longer accept it.

sentences.zh: 須臾，敕希烈推之。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Xilie to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict ordered Xilie to investigate.

sentences.zh: 鉷以表示宰相，林甫曰：「大夫後之矣。」

translations.literal: Hong showed the memorial to the chief minister; Linfu said: 'Grandee, you are too late.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hong showed the memorial to the chief minister. Linfu said, 'Grandee, you are too late.'"

sentences.zh: 遂不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 俄銲至，國忠問：「大夫知否？」

translations.literal: Soon Han arrived; Guozhong asked: 'Does the Grandee know?'"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Han arrived. Guozhong asked, 'Do you know, Grandee?'"

sentences.zh: 銲未及應。

translations.literal: Han had not yet answered.
translations.idiomatic: Han had not yet answered.

sentences.zh: 侍御史裴冕恐銲引之，冕叱詈之曰：「足下為臣不忠，為弟不義。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Pei Mian, fearing Han would implicate him, shouted and reviled him, saying: 'You, sir, as minister are disloyal, as younger brother unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Pei Mian, fearing Han would implicate Hong, shouted at him, 'You are disloyal as a minister and unrighteous as a younger brother.

sentences.zh: 聖上以大夫之故，以足下為戶部郎中，又加五品，恩亦厚矣。

translations.literal: Because of the Grandee the sage ruler made you Director of the Ministry of Revenue and additionally raised you five ranks—the grace is also thick.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the Grandee the sage ruler made you director of the Ministry of Revenue and raised you five ranks—the grace was great.

sentences.zh: 大夫豈知縡事乎？」

translations.literal: Did the Grandee know of Zao's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Did the Grandee know of Zao's affair?"

sentences.zh: 國忠愕然，謂銲曰：「實知，即不可隱；

translations.literal: Guozhong was startled and said to Han: 'If you truly know, then it cannot be concealed;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was startled and said to Han, 'If you truly know, you cannot conceal it.

sentences.zh: 不知，亦不可妄引。」

translations.literal: if you do not know, you also cannot falsely implicate.'"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not know, you must not falsely implicate him.'"

sentences.zh: 銲方曰：「七兄不知。」

translations.literal: Han then said: 'Seventh Brother did not know.'"
translations.idiomatic: Han then said, 'Seventh Brother did not know.'"

sentences.zh: 季鄰證其罪。

translations.literal: Jilin testified to his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin testified to his guilt.

sentences.zh: 及日暮，奏之。

translations.literal: When evening came, the report was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When evening came, the report was submitted.

sentences.zh: 銲決杖死於朝堂，賜鉷自盡於三衛廚。

translations.literal: Han was sentenced to death by beating in the court hall; Hong was granted self-extermination in the Three Guards kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Han was beaten to death in the court hall; Hong was granted self-extermination in the Three Guards kitchen.

sentences.zh: 明日，移於資聖寺廊下，裴冕言於國忠，令歸宅權斂之，又請令妻、女送墓所，國忠義而許之，令鉷判官齊奇營護之。

translations.literal: The next day he was moved beneath the corridor of Zisheng Temple; Pei Mian spoke to Guozhong, ordering return to the residence for provisional encoffining, again requesting that wife and daughters be sent to the tomb site—Guozhong, deeming it righteous, permitted it and ordered Hong's assistant official Qi Qi to arrange and protect the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hong's body was moved beneath the corridor of Zisheng Temple. Pei Mian asked Guozhong to allow temporary encoffining at home and that wife and daughters be sent to the tomb. Guozhong, deeming it righteous, permitted it and ordered Hong's assistant official Qi Qi to arrange matters.

sentences.zh: 男準除名，長流嶺南承化郡，備長流珠崖郡，至故驛殺之；

translations.literal: The son Zhun was removed from the register and long exiled to Chenghua Commandery in Lingnan; Bei long exiled to Zhuya Commandery—at the old post station they were killed;
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Zhun was removed from the register and long exiled to Chenghua Commandery in Lingnan; Bei was long exiled to Zhuya Commandery. At the old post station they were killed.

sentences.zh: 妻薛氏及在室女並流。

translations.literal: Wife the Xue clan and unmarried daughters were all exiled.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, of the Xue clan, and unmarried daughters were all exiled.

sentences.zh: 初，鉷與御史中丞、戶部侍郎楊慎矜親，且情厚，頗為汲引，及貴盛爭權，鉷附於李林甫，為所誘，陷慎矜家。

translations.literal: At first Hong was close to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Shenjin, and their affection was thick; he had greatly promoted and recommended him. When both were noble and contended for power, Hong attached himself to Li Linfu, was tempted by him, and trapped the Shenjin family.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hong was close to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Shenjin and had greatly promoted him. When both rose and contended for power, Hong attached himself to Li Linfu, was tempted by him, and destroyed the Shenjin family.

sentences.zh: 經五年而鉷至赤族，豈天道歟！

translations.literal: After five years Hong reached extinction of his clan—is this not Heaven's way!
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Hong's clan was extinguished—is this not Heaven's way!

sentences.zh: 【贊】=史臣曰：夫奸佞之輩，惟事悅人；

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: Treacherous and flattering sorts serve only to please others;
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian says: Treacherous flatterers serve only to please others;

sentences.zh: 聚斂之臣，無非害物。

translations.literal: ministers who amass wealth never fail to harm things.
translations.idiomatic: ministers who amass wealth invariably harm the people.

sentences.zh: 賈禍招怨，敗國喪身，罕不由斯道也。

translations.literal: Inviting calamity and drawing resentment, ruining the state and losing one's life—few do not follow this path.
translations.idiomatic: Inviting calamity and drawing resentment, ruining the state and losing one's life—few escape this path.

sentences.zh: 君人者，中智已降，亦心緣利動，言為甘聞，誌雖慕於聖明，情不勝於嗜欲，徒有賢佐，無如之何，所以禮經戒其勿畜。

translations.literal: For rulers, from middling intelligence downward, the heart is also moved by profit, words are sweet to hear; though the will admires sages, feeling cannot overcome craving—though there are worthy assistants, nothing can be done about it. Therefore the Book of Rites warns against keeping such men.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of middling intelligence and below are moved by profit and love sweet words. Though they admire the sages, appetite overcomes intent; even worthy assistants cannot restrain them. The Book of Rites therefore warns against keeping such men.

sentences.zh: 宇文融、韋堅、楊慎矜、王鉷，皆開元之幸人也，或以括戶取媚，或以漕運承恩，或以聚貨得權，或以剝下獲寵，負勢自用，人莫敢違。

translations.literal: Yu Wenrong, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, and Wang Hong were all favored men of the Kaiyuan era—some pleasing by registering households, some receiving grace through canal transport, some gaining power through amassing goods, some winning favor through stripping those below. Bearing power they acted as they pleased, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenrong, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, and Wang Hong were all favorites of the Kaiyuan era—some by registering households, some by canal transport, some by amassing wealth, some by stripping those below. Empowered, they did as they pleased, and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 張說、李林甫手握大權，承主恩顧，尚遭淩擯，以身下之，他人即可知也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue and Li Linfu held great power and received the ruler's favor, yet still suffered bullying and had to lower themselves—others can be known from this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue and Li Linfu held great power and imperial favor, yet still suffered bullying and had to yield. Others may be judged by the same measure.

sentences.zh: 然天道惡盈，器滿則覆，終雖不令，其弊已多，良可痛也。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's way hates fullness; when the vessel is full it overturns. Though the end was not good, the harm was already great— truly painful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven hates excess; when the vessel is full it overturns. Though their ends were unhappy, the harm was already great— truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 宋璟、裴耀卿、許景先獲居重任，因融薦之，此亦有鳳之一毛也。

translations.literal: Song Jing, Pei Yaoqing, and Xu Jingxian obtained heavy responsibilities because Rong recommended them—this too is one feather of the phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing, Pei Yaoqing, and Xu Jingxian obtained heavy responsibilities through Rong's recommendation—this too counts as one feather of the phoenix.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以聖哲之姿，處高明之位，未免此累，或承之羞，後之帝王，得不深鑒！

translations.literal: Xuanzong with sage wisdom's bearing, occupying the high and bright position, still could not avoid this burden—perhaps a shame to inherit; later emperors—can they not deeply take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, with sage wisdom and in the highest seat, still could not escape this burden—a warning to those who follow. Later emperors should take deep heed!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：財能域人，聚則民散。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wealth can bound men; when gathered, the people scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wealth can confine men; when gathered, the people scatter.

sentences.zh: 如何帝王，誌求餘羨。

translations.literal: How is it that emperors, in will, seek surplus profit?
translations.idiomatic: Why do emperors in will seek surplus profit?

sentences.zh: 融、堅、矜、鉷，因利乘便。

translations.literal: Rong, Jian, Shenjin, and Hong, riding profit and seizing opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, Jian, Shenjin, and Hong rode profit and seized opportunity.

sentences.zh: 以僥寵榮，宜招後患。

translations.literal: By chance winning favor and glory, they should invite later calamity.
translations.idiomatic: By chance winning favor and glory, they were bound to invite later calamity.
